answer.narration:
"I'll take it." Juno grins and cuts the call.

Bay Nine is cold and smells of coolant. It's crammed with three stubby courier skiffs, and one of them is scarred along the belly like it has scraped a few ledges already. Juno meets you at the hatch and slaps a sealed white crate strapped in the cargo net.

"Insulin and antibiotics. The ridge hab's out of both." She hands you a datapad with the approach chart. "Crosswinds don't exist on Ceres, but the dust does. Kicks up off the pad and blinds your sensors at the last fifty metres. Last guy bent a strut."

The skiff's controls are worn smooth. Your hands settle on them like they've always lived there.

answer.summary: Waren Spacefarer, a young pilot with ten credits, wants forty thousand to buy Marta Okafor's Kestrel. His relief pilot job on Dren Vasko's tug Grubstake turned out to be people smuggling. He alerted customs, disabled the drive, got Vasko to surrender and freed eleven refugees. He gave Inspector Hale an honest statement, filed an informant fund claim (payout months away) and had his ribs strapped. The Vesta job is probably lost. He accepted Juno Reyes's three-hundred-credit courier run with medicine to Occator Ridge and is now in her skiff at Bay Nine. The ridge pad is a dusty ledge that blinds sensors. Juno hints at steadier, better-paid work afterwards.
